builder-mindset-story.text: The Old Way. AJ is leaning back with Nia and Malik after school, watching the old rule play out again: people act like building real things means years of coding, expensive courses, and waiting for permission. That old way kept the door narrow for too long.
The New Reality. Then Nia spots the shift. With AI, the crew can describe an idea in plain English and get a real first build back fast. The lane opens, and AJ sees the door swing wider.
Step 1: Think It. AJ starts where every good build starts: what would actually help somebody? What problem is worth fixing, and who needs it most?
Step 2: Describe It. Malik pushes AJ to say it clearly. If the idea is blurry, the build will be blurry. The words have to do real work before the code ever shows up.

Step 3: AI Builds It. The model turns the crew's description into working code, and now the idea has a shape they can test. AJ sees the first version and knows the story just turned into something real.
Step 4: It's Live!. AJ puts it online and the crew reacts like they just crossed a line. They are not just using the internet anymore. They built something people can touch, share, and improve.

art-of-building-story.text: Building is a Conversation. AJ learns that building with AI feels like trading notes with a sharp assistant. He talks, Nia reacts, Malik tests, and the next version gets better because the whole crew stays in the loop.
Describe What You Want. Nia keeps AJ honest: describe the thing with enough detail that the machine can see the shape of it and start moving with purpose.
Preview the Result. Malik opens the preview and looks for what landed and what missed. The first look tells the truth before anybody starts pretending it is finished.
Ask for Changes. AJ does not defend the first draft. He asks for changes, gets specific, and uses feedback to tighten the build until the team feels it.
Keep Iterating. The crew keeps looping. Good builders do not chase perfection on round one. They use each round to get closer, cleaner, and sharper.

clear-prompts-story.text: Description Quality Matters. AJ learns that the quality of the build tracks directly with the quality of the prompt. When the words are loose, the result is loose. When the words are sharp, the build gets sharp right along with them.
Too Vague. AJ says, 'make me a website,' and Nia laughs because that is not a prompt, that is a wish. The AI can only guess when the setup stays that vague.
Say WHAT It Is. So AJ names the thing: a quiz page about Grand Rapids history. Now the model knows the kind of build, the topic, and the lane it has to stay in.
List the Features. Malik adds the features: five multiple choice questions, instant feedback, a score, a try-again button. Now the build has a job and a clean finish line.
Describe the Style. Nia finishes the prompt with the style: modern, blue, clean, easy to move through. The result starts matching the vision instead of drifting away from it.
